method: Placements are editorial judgements from laws and records on a 0–100 scale per axis. See the Method page of the Twelve-Point Compass.

leaders.name: Donald Trump
leaders.summary: Republican president whose two terms combined tax cuts and deregulation with broad tariffs, tight immigration enforcement and withdrawal from international agreements.

record.event: Signed the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, cutting the corporate tax rate from 35% to 21%
Announced US withdrawal from the Paris climate agreement
Imposed tariffs on imported steel and aluminium
Imposed broad “reciprocal” tariffs on most trading partners
Ordered withdrawal from the World Health Organization and, again, from the Paris agreement
Launched a mass-deportation drive and deployed the National Guard to Los Angeles and Washington
Ordered strikes on Iranian nuclear sites
US forces captured Venezuela’s president Nicolás Maduro

leaders.name: Xi Jinping
leaders.role: General Secretary of the Communist Party and President of China
leaders.summary: Has concentrated power in the party and in his own office, tightened control of society and private business, and expanded China’s global economic reach.

record.event: Launched the Belt and Road Initiative of overseas infrastructure lending
Launched Made in China 2025, an industrial policy for home-grown high technology
Mass detention of Uyghurs in Xinjiang camps began, later documented by the UN human rights office (2022)
Presidential term limits removed from the constitution
Hong Kong National Security Law imposed
Pledged carbon neutrality by 2060
“Common prosperity” drive and crackdown on large technology firms

leaders.name: Narendra Modi
leaders.summary: BJP prime minister who combined market reforms and large welfare transfers with Hindu-nationalist politics and more centralised government.

record.event: Withdrew 500 and 1,000 rupee notes overnight (demonetisation)
Introduced a national Goods and Services Tax
Revoked Jammu and Kashmir’s special status under Article 370
Citizenship Amendment Act fast-tracked citizenship for non-Muslim refugees from three neighbours
Kept India out of the RCEP Asian trade pact
Led the consecration of the Ram temple in Ayodhya
Ordered Operation Sindoor strikes on Pakistan

leaders.name: Vladimir Putin
leaders.summary: Has dominated Russia for a quarter of a century, closing down political competition, promoting conservative values and waging wars against Georgia and Ukraine.

record.event: As prime minister, oversaw the war with Georgia
Signed the law banning “propaganda of non-traditional sexual relations” to minors
Annexed Crimea from Ukraine
Constitutional amendments allowed him two further terms
Launched the full-scale invasion of Ukraine
Laws criminalised “discrediting” or spreading “false information” about the army
Supreme Court declared the “international LGBT movement” extremist

leaders.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
leaders.summary: Former actor elected on an anti-corruption platform who has led Ukraine’s defence against the Russian invasion and its bid to join the EU.

record.event: Elected president with 73% in the run-off
Opened the market in farmland
Led national defence under martial law after Russia’s invasion; elections suspended under martial law
Ukraine ratified the Istanbul Convention on violence against women
Ukraine granted EU candidate status
Signed, then reversed after street protests, a law curbing anti-corruption agencies

leaders.name: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
leaders.summary: Workers’ Party president known for cash-transfer anti-poverty programmes and multilateral diplomacy; re-elected for a fourth term in October 2026.
leaders.note: Re-elected 25 October 2026; the new term begins 1 January 2027.

record.event: Created Bolsa Família, cash transfers to poor families tied to schooling and health checks
Relaunched Bolsa Família on returning to office
Amazon deforestation fell by about half in his first year back
Hosted the COP30 climate summit in Belém
Won the presidential run-off against Flávio Bolsonaro with about 52%

leaders.name: Claudia Sheinbaum
leaders.summary: Morena president and former climate scientist continuing her predecessor’s state-led energy policy, social programmes and judicial overhaul.

record.event: Became Mexico’s first woman president
Took office as a judicial reform making judges popularly elected came into force
Mexico held its first popular election of judges
Proposed tariffs of up to 50% on imports from countries without trade deals with Mexico, including China
Expanded cash pensions and transfers

leaders.name: Javier Milei
leaders.summary: Self-described anarcho-capitalist economist who has cut public spending sharply, deregulated by decree and is socially conservative.

record.event: Cut the number of ministries from 18 to 9
Decree 70/2023 repealed or changed hundreds of economic rules
Congress passed his “Bases” reform law
Argentina posted its first annual fiscal surplus since 2010
Announced Argentina’s withdrawal from the World Health Organization

leaders.name: Mark Carney
leaders.summary: Liberal prime minister and former central banker who has prioritised trade defence against the US, faster infrastructure approvals and higher defence spending.

record.event: Governor of the Bank of Canada (2008–2013), then of the Bank of England (2013–2020)
Ended the consumer carbon tax on his first day in office
Kept and extended counter-tariffs on US goods
Building Canada Act fast-tracked major national projects
Committed to NATO’s target of 5% of GDP on defence by 2035

leaders.name: Andy Burnham
leaders.role: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom
leaders.summary: Labour prime minister since July 2026, previously Mayor of Greater Manchester, known for bringing buses back under public control and for championing devolution.
leaders.note: Placement leans on his record as mayor; his record as prime minister is only a few months old.

record.event: Health Secretary in Gordon Brown’s government
Elected first Mayor of Greater Manchester
Brought Greater Manchester’s buses back under public control (Bee Network)
Elected Labour leader unopposed and appointed prime minister on 20 July

leaders.name: Emmanuel Macron
leaders.summary: Centrist president who liberalised labour law, raised the pension age, and pushed for deeper European integration and defence.

record.event: Labour-market reform by government ordinance
A fuel tax rise set off the gilets jaunes protests; it was suspended
Law against “separatism” to enforce secular principles
Raised the pension age from 62 to 64, bypassing a final vote in parliament
Immigration law tightened rules on benefits and removals
Freedom to have an abortion written into the constitution

leaders.name: Friedrich Merz
leaders.summary: Christian Democrat chancellor who loosened the debt brake for defence and infrastructure and tightened border controls on asylum.

record.event: Won a parliamentary motion to tighten migration rules with votes from the AfD
Exempted most defence spending from the debt brake and created a €500 billion infrastructure fund
His government ordered asylum seekers turned back at the border

leaders.name: Giorgia Meloni
leaders.summary: Brothers of Italy leader governing as a national conservative: firm on migration and family policy, cooperative with the EU and NATO.

record.event: Became Italy’s first woman prime minister
Signed a deal to process migrants in centres in Albania
Replaced the “citizens’ income” with a narrower inclusion allowance
Senate passed her constitutional bill for a directly elected prime minister
Surrogacy abroad made a crime for Italians

leaders.name: Pedro Sánchez
leaders.summary: Socialist prime minister who raised the minimum wage, legislated socially progressive laws and governs with regional parties.

record.event: Came to power through a vote of no confidence
Legalised euthanasia
Raised the minimum wage by more than half between 2018 and 2025
Amnesty law for those involved in the Catalan independence push
Recognised the State of Palestine
Secured an exemption from NATO’s 5% defence-spending target

leaders.name: Sanae Takaichi
leaders.summary: Conservative LDP prime minister, a protégée of Shinzo Abe, hawkish on China and on defence, with a two-thirds majority since February 2026.

record.event: Became Japan’s first woman prime minister
Said a Taiwan emergency could threaten Japan’s survival, prompting a diplomatic row with China
Won a two-thirds majority in a snap lower-house election
Long opposed letting married couples keep separate surnames
Has regularly visited the Yasukuni Shrine as a lawmaker

leaders.name: Lee Jae-myung
leaders.summary: Democratic Party president elected after his predecessor’s removal over a martial-law decree; an advocate of basic income and talks with the North.

record.event: As Gyeonggi governor, introduced a basic income for 24-year-olds
Led opposition to the December martial-law declaration and the impeachment that followed
Won the snap presidential election
Halted loudspeaker broadcasts at the border with North Korea

leaders.name: Prabowo Subianto
leaders.summary: Former general whose government has expanded the state’s economic role, launched free school meals and widened the military’s place in civilian life.

record.event: Discharged from the army after an inquiry into the abduction of activists
Launched free nutritious meals for schoolchildren
Created the Danantara sovereign wealth fund to hold state companies
Indonesia joined BRICS
Revised military law let serving officers hold more civilian posts

leaders.name: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan
leaders.summary: Has led Turkey for over two decades, moving it to an executive presidency, a more religious public life and a strongly independent foreign policy.

record.event: Mass purges and emergency rule after a failed coup attempt
Referendum created an executive presidency
Hagia Sophia reconverted into a mosque
Withdrew Turkey from the Istanbul Convention on violence against women
Istanbul’s opposition mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu arrested

leaders.name: Mohammed bin Salman
leaders.role: Crown Prince and Prime Minister of Saudi Arabia
leaders.summary: De facto ruler who has loosened social rules and pursued state-led economic diversification while tolerating no dissent.

record.event: As defence minister, launched the Saudi-led intervention in Yemen
Announced Vision 2030 economic diversification; the religious police lost arrest powers
Hundreds of princes and businessmen detained at the Ritz-Carlton in an anti-corruption drive
Women allowed to drive
Journalist Jamal Khashoggi killed in the Saudi consulate in Istanbul; US intelligence later assessed the crown prince approved the operation

leaders.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
leaders.summary: ANC president governing in a coalition since 2024, pursuing national health insurance and land reform alongside market-friendly economics.

record.event: South Africa brought a genocide case against Israel at the International Court of Justice
Signed the National Health Insurance Act
Formed a Government of National Unity after the ANC lost its majority
Signed the Expropriation Act, allowing expropriation without compensation in limited cases

leaders.name: Bola Tinubu
leaders.summary: APC president who scrapped the petrol subsidy and floated the naira, and has used emergency powers against a state government.

record.event: Governor of Lagos State (1999–2007)
Ended the petrol subsidy on taking office
Unified exchange rates, letting the naira float
Declared emergency rule in Rivers State, suspending its governor

leaders.name: Abdel Fattah el-Sisi
leaders.summary: Former army chief who took power after removing President Morsi; his rule has seen sweeping repression and military-led megaprojects.

record.event: As army chief, led the removal of President Mohamed Morsi
Security forces killed hundreds of protesters at Rabaa al-Adawiya square
Opened the New Suez Canal expansion
Constitutional amendments extended his rule to 2030

leaders.name: Abiy Ahmed
leaders.summary: Won the Nobel Peace Prize for ending the war with Eritrea, then fought a devastating war in Tigray; his Prosperity Party won a landslide in 2026.

record.event: Made peace with Eritrea; awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2019
Merged the ruling coalition into the single Prosperity Party
Launched the Green Legacy tree-planting campaign
War in Tigray (2020–2022)
Floated the birr under an IMF programme
Prosperity Party won 438 of 547 seats

leaders.name: Anthony Albanese
leaders.summary: Labor prime minister who legislated an emissions target, held the failed Voice referendum and kept the AUKUS submarine deal.

record.event: Legislated a 43% emissions cut by 2030
Referendum on an Indigenous Voice to Parliament was defeated
Banned social media accounts for under-16s
Re-elected with a larger majority
Kept the AUKUS nuclear-submarine partnership

leaders.name: Kim Jong Un
leaders.summary: Third-generation ruler of a closed one-party state who has expanded its nuclear arsenal and sent troops to fight for Russia.

record.event: Had his uncle Jang Song-thaek executed
Tested a thermonuclear device and intercontinental missiles
Held summits with South Korea’s Moon Jae-in and US President Trump
Sent troops to fight for Russia against Ukraine

leaders.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
leaders.summary: Israel’s longest-serving prime minister: a free-marketeer and security hawk who has governed with religious and nationalist parties.
leaders.note: Israel voted on 27 October 2026; final results and a new government were still pending when this was checked.

record.event: As finance minister (2003–2005), cut spending and privatised state firms
Nation-State Law defined Israel as the nation state of the Jewish people
Pushed a judicial overhaul; the Supreme Court struck down its first law in January 2024
Led the war in Gaza after the 7 October Hamas attack
International Criminal Court issued an arrest warrant for him
Ordered strikes on Iran

leaders.name: Donald Tusk
leaders.summary: Centre-right liberal and former President of the European Council, focused on EU ties, rule of law, defence and a hard line at the Belarus border.

record.event: President of the European Council (2014–2019)
Took over public media from the previous government
Law allowing asylum applications to be suspended at the Belarus border
Defence spending above 4% of GDP, the highest in NATO

leaders.name: Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
leaders.summary: Son of the former dictator; has moved the Philippines closer to the US in the South China Sea and allowed his predecessor’s arrest for the ICC.

record.event: Gave the US military access to four more Philippine bases
Created the Maharlika sovereign wealth fund
Former president Rodrigo Duterte was arrested and handed to the International Criminal Court

leaders.name: Nayib Bukele
leaders.summary: Crushed gang violence through a long state of emergency and mass detention, made Bitcoin legal tender and removed limits on re-election.

record.event: Made Bitcoin legal tender
Declared a state of exception against gangs; tens of thousands detained
Opened the CECOT mega-prison
Re-elected despite a constitutional bar on consecutive terms
Congress approved indefinite re-election

leaders.name: José Antonio Kast
leaders.summary: Founder of the Republican Party, elected on promises of security, deportations and smaller government; Chile’s sharpest turn to the right since 1990.
leaders.note: In office since March 2026: placement leans on his platform and party record.

record.event: Founded the Republican Party
Lost the presidential run-off to Gabriel Boric
Won the presidential run-off; sworn in on 11 March 2026
Campaigned on border barriers and expelling undocumented migrants
Opposes abortion

leaders.name: Keiko Fujimori
leaders.summary: Daughter of former president Alberto Fujimori and leader of Popular Force; elected in 2026 on her fourth attempt on a law-and-order, pro-market platform.
leaders.note: New in office: placement is from her party’s platform and record in Congress.

record.event: Founded the Popular Force party
Lost run-offs in 2011, 2016 and 2021
Won the June 2026 run-off

leaders.name: Abelardo de la Espriella
leaders.summary: Right-wing populist lawyer who narrowly won the June 2026 run-off promising a hard line against armed groups.
leaders.note: New in office: placement is from his campaign platform.

record.event: Won the run-off with 49.7% against Iván Cepeda; sworn in on 7 August
Campaigned on a hard line against armed groups and crime

leaders.name: Tarique Rahman
leaders.summary: BNP leader and son of two former heads of state, sworn in after his party’s landslide in an election the Awami League was barred from.
leaders.note: New in office: placement is from the BNP’s platform and record.

record.event: Left for London, where he lived for nearly two decades
Sworn in on 17 February after the BNP’s election landslide

leaders.name: Anutin Charnvirakul
leaders.summary: Bhumjaithai leader who, as health minister, took cannabis off Thailand’s narcotics list; re-elected prime minister after his party came first in 2026.

record.event: As health minister, removed cannabis from the narcotics list
Became prime minister
Re-elected prime minister by the new parliament after Bhumjaithai won the most seats

leaders.name: Shehbaz Sharif
leaders.summary: PML-N prime minister governing in close alliance with the army, under an IMF programme.

record.event: Became prime minister after Imran Khan lost a no-confidence vote
Agreed a $7 billion IMF programme
26th constitutional amendment changed how senior judges are appointed
Military clashes with India in May

leaders.name: Péter Magyar
leaders.summary: Former Fidesz insider whose Tisza party ended Viktor Orbán’s 16-year rule in April 2026 on a pro-EU, anti-corruption platform.
leaders.note: New in office: placement is from Tisza’s platform.

record.event: Led the new Tisza party to second place in the European elections
Won a two-thirds majority on 12 April; sworn in on 9 May
Pledged to fight corruption and unlock frozen EU funds

leaders.name: Rob Jetten
leaders.summary: D66 social liberal and former climate minister, the youngest Dutch prime minister, leading a minority centrist coalition.

record.event: Minister for Climate and Energy (2022–2024)
D66 won the most votes in the October election
Sworn in on 23 February with a D66, VVD and CDA cabinet

leaders.name: Ursula von der Leyen
leaders.summary: German Christian Democrat leading the EU executive through the Green Deal, joint pandemic borrowing and European rearmament.

record.event: German defence minister (2013–2019)
Launched the European Green Deal
NextGenerationEU recovery fund financed by joint EU borrowing
EU adopted the Pact on Migration and Asylum
Proposed the ReArm Europe defence plan

leaders.name: Keir Starmer
leaders.role: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom
leaders.summary: Labour prime minister elected in a 2024 landslide who resigned in June 2026 after heavy local-election losses.

record.event: Created Great British Energy, a publicly owned clean-power company
Cut winter fuel payments for most pensioners, later partly reversed
Committed to raise defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2027
Proscribed the group Palestine Action as a terrorist organisation
Resigned after Labour’s losses in the May local elections

leaders.name: Viktor Orbán
leaders.summary: Built what he called an “illiberal democracy”: a new constitution, tight migration control, conservative family policy and friction with the EU.

record.event: New constitution passed with his party’s two-thirds majority
Built a fence on the southern border against migrants
Law banning content that “promotes” homosexuality to minors
Ban on Pride marches
Lost the April election to Péter Magyar’s Tisza

leaders.name: Gustavo Petro
leaders.summary: Former M-19 guerrilla who became Colombia’s first left-wing president, halting new oil exploration and pursuing talks with armed groups.

record.event: Mayor of Bogotá (2012–2015)
Stopped signing new oil and gas exploration contracts
“Total Peace” negotiations with armed groups

leaders.name: Nicolás Maduro
leaders.summary: Chávez’s successor, whose rule saw economic collapse, mass emigration and disputed elections, until US forces captured him in January 2026.

record.event: Created a Constituent Assembly that sidelined the opposition-led parliament
Declared winner of the presidential election without published polling-station tallies
More than 7 million Venezuelans emigrated during his rule
Captured by US forces in January

leaders.name: Ali Khamenei
leaders.summary: Supreme Leader for 37 years, the final authority over Iran’s clerical system; killed in US-Israeli strikes in February 2026 and succeeded by his son Mojtaba.

record.event: Backed the crackdown on the Green Movement protests
Allowed the nuclear deal with world powers
Backed the crackdown on protests after the death of Mahsa Amini
Killed in US-Israeli strikes on 28 February

leaders.name: Joe Biden
leaders.summary: Democratic president who passed large spending packages on recovery, infrastructure, chips and clean energy, and kept many tariffs.

record.event: Signed the American Rescue Plan
Rejoined the Paris agreement
Completed the withdrawal from Afghanistan
Inflation Reduction Act funded clean energy
CHIPS Act subsidised home chip-making
Signed the Respect for Marriage Act

leaders.name: Barack Obama
leaders.summary: Democratic president who passed the Affordable Care Act, signed the Paris and Iran agreements, and expanded drone warfare.

record.event: Signed the Affordable Care Act
Ordered the raid that killed Osama bin Laden; joined the intervention in Libya
DACA shielded young undocumented immigrants from deportation
Endorsed same-sex marriage
Joined the Paris agreement and the Iran nuclear deal

leaders.name: Angela Merkel
leaders.summary: Christian Democrat chancellor through the eurozone crisis and the 2015 refugee arrivals, and the architect of Germany’s nuclear phase-out.

record.event: Tied eurozone bailouts to austerity conditions
Decided to phase out nuclear power after Fukushima
Kept borders open as more than a million asylum seekers arrived
Allowed a free vote that legalised same-sex marriage, though she voted against

leaders.name: Jacinda Ardern
leaders.summary: Labour prime minister known for the gun ban after the Christchurch attack, a zero-carbon law and strict pandemic border closures.

record.event: Banned most semi-automatic weapons after the Christchurch mosque attacks
Passed the Zero Carbon Act
First “Wellbeing Budget”
Closed the borders to eliminate COVID-19

leaders.name: Shinzo Abe
leaders.summary: Japan’s longest-serving prime minister: “Abenomics”, a reinterpreted pacifist constitution and nationalist conservatism.

record.event: Launched “Abenomics” monetary easing, stimulus and reform
Visited the Yasukuni Shrine
Security laws allowed collective self-defence
Signed the CPTPP trade pact
Assassinated while campaigning

leaders.name: Bernie Sanders
leaders.summary: Independent democratic socialist and twice a candidate for the Democratic presidential nomination, campaigning for Medicare for All.

record.event: Mayor of Burlington, Vermont (1981–1989)
Voted against NAFTA
Voted against the Iraq war
Ran for president on Medicare for All and free public college

leaders.name: Marine Le Pen
leaders.summary: Led her father’s Front National into the mainstream as the National Rally, campaigning on immigration and economic protection.

record.event: Took over the Front National, renamed National Rally in 2018
Reached the presidential run-off in 2017 and 2022
Proposes “national priority” for citizens in jobs and housing
Convicted at first instance of embezzling EU parliamentary funds and barred from standing for office; she appealed

leaders.name: Alexei Navalny
leaders.summary: Russia’s best-known opposition figure, who exposed official corruption and died in an Arctic penal colony in 2024.

record.event: Founded the Anti-Corruption Foundation
Won 27% in the Moscow mayoral election
Poisoned with a Novichok nerve agent
Imprisoned on his return to Russia
Died in prison

leaders.name: Imran Khan
leaders.role: Founder of PTI; Prime Minister of Pakistan 2018–2022
leaders.summary: Former cricket captain whose government expanded welfare and tree-planting; removed by parliament in 2022 and jailed since 2023.

record.event: Founded Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf
Ten Billion Tree Tsunami programme
Ehsaas social protection programme
Removed by a no-confidence vote
Imprisoned

leaders.name: Rahul Gandhi
leaders.role: Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha
leaders.summary: Congress leader and India’s opposition leader since 2024, campaigning on welfare, caste census and constitutional rights.

record.event: President of the Indian National Congress (2017–2019)
Bharat Jodo Yatra, a march across India
Disqualified from parliament after a defamation conviction, reinstated when the Supreme Court stayed it
Became Leader of the Opposition

leaders.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
leaders.summary: Four-term president of the New Deal and the Second World War.

record.event: New Deal programmes of relief, public works and bank regulation
Social Security Act
Tried to enlarge the Supreme Court
Lend-Lease aid to Britain and allies
Ordered the internment of Japanese Americans

leaders.name: Winston Churchill
leaders.role: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom
leaders.summary: Conservative wartime leader against Nazi Germany and a defender of the British Empire.

record.event: Led Britain through the Second World War
Signed the Atlantic Charter with Roosevelt
“Iron Curtain” speech
Opposed Indian independence

leaders.name: Clement Attlee
leaders.role: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom
leaders.summary: Labour prime minister who founded the National Health Service and nationalised major industries.

record.event: Nationalised coal, then rail, electricity and gas
Granted independence to India and Pakistan
Founded the National Health Service
Founding member of NATO

leaders.name: Charles de Gaulle
leaders.summary: Leader of Free France who founded the Fifth Republic with a strong presidency and an independent foreign policy.

record.event: Led Free France from London
Fifth Republic constitution with a strong presidency
Accepted Algerian independence
Withdrew France from NATO’s integrated command

leaders.name: Konrad Adenauer
leaders.summary: First West German chancellor, a Christian Democrat who anchored Germany in the West and in European integration.

record.event: Social market economy with Ludwig Erhard
West Germany joined NATO
Signed the Treaty of Rome founding the EEC
Élysée Treaty with France

leaders.name: Margaret Thatcher
leaders.role: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom
leaders.summary: Conservative prime minister of privatisation, union reform and the Falklands War.

record.event: Falklands War
Privatised British Telecom, then gas, water and electricity
Faced down the year-long miners’ strike
Abolished the Greater London Council
Section 28 banned the “promotion” of homosexuality by councils

leaders.name: Ronald Reagan
leaders.summary: Republican president of tax cuts, a Cold War arms build-up and, later, nuclear arms reduction.

record.event: Large income tax cuts
Fired striking air traffic controllers
Launched the Strategic Defense Initiative
Signed an immigration law that legalised about three million people
Signed the INF nuclear treaty with the Soviet Union

leaders.name: Mikhail Gorbachev
leaders.summary: Last Soviet leader, whose openness and reforms ended the Cold War and, unintentionally, the Soviet Union.

record.event: Glasnost (openness) and perestroika (restructuring)
Signed the INF nuclear treaty
Did not intervene as Eastern Europe’s communist regimes fell
Awarded the Nobel Peace Prize

leaders.name: Vladimir Lenin
leaders.summary: Bolshevik leader of the October Revolution and founder of the Soviet one-party state.

record.event: Led the October Revolution
Dissolved the elected Constituent Assembly; the Cheka’s Red Terror
New Economic Policy allowed limited private trade
Founded the Soviet Union

leaders.name: Joseph Stalin
leaders.summary: Turned the Soviet Union into a totalitarian industrial power through forced collectivisation, purges and the Gulag.

record.event: First Five-Year Plan and forced collectivisation; famine in 1932–33
The Great Purge
Pact with Nazi Germany
Led the Soviet war against Germany
Deported whole nationalities

leaders.name: Mao Zedong
leaders.role: Chairman of the Chinese Communist Party
leaders.summary: Founder of the People’s Republic whose Great Leap Forward caused one of history’s worst famines.

record.event: Proclaimed the People’s Republic of China
Sent Chinese forces into the Korean War
Great Leap Forward; famine to 1962
Launched the Cultural Revolution
Received US President Nixon

leaders.name: Deng Xiaoping
leaders.summary: Opened China’s economy to markets and foreign investment while keeping one-party rule.

record.event: Launched “reform and opening up”
Created the Shenzhen special economic zone; the one-child policy began
Ordered the Tiananmen Square crackdown
Southern tour relaunched market reforms

leaders.name: Mahatma Gandhi
leaders.role: Leader of the Indian independence movement
leaders.summary: Led India’s non-violent struggle for independence and championed village self-reliance.

record.event: Non-cooperation movement
Salt March against the British salt tax
Quit India movement
Swadeshi: home-spun cloth and boycott of British goods
Assassinated

leaders.name: Jawaharlal Nehru
leaders.summary: India’s first prime minister: parliamentary democracy, state planning, secularism and non-alignment.

record.event: First Five-Year Plan
Hindu Code Bills reformed marriage and inheritance
Co-founded the Non-Aligned Movement
War with China

leaders.name: Indira Gandhi
leaders.summary: Nationalised banks, won the 1971 war that created Bangladesh, and ruled by decree during the Emergency.

record.event: Nationalised 14 major banks
War with Pakistan led to the creation of Bangladesh
India’s first nuclear test
Declared a State of Emergency, suspending elections and civil liberties until 1977
Assassinated after Operation Blue Star

leaders.name: Atal Bihari Vajpayee
leaders.summary: First BJP prime minister to serve a full term: nuclear tests, privatisation and peace overtures to Pakistan.

record.event: Pokhran-II nuclear tests
Bus diplomacy to Lahore; the Kargil war followed
Created a ministry to sell state companies

leaders.name: Nelson Mandela
leaders.summary: Anti-apartheid leader imprisoned for 27 years who became South Africa’s first democratically elected president and served one term.

record.event: Co-founded the ANC’s armed wing, Umkhonto we Sizwe
Imprisoned until 1990
Set up the Truth and Reconciliation Commission
Signed a constitution protecting against discrimination including on sexual orientation
Stepped down after one term

leaders.name: Gamal Abdel Nasser
leaders.role: Prime Minister, then President of Egypt
leaders.summary: Pan-Arab nationalist who nationalised the Suez Canal and built a one-party state.

record.event: Led the Free Officers’ coup
Land reform
Nationalised the Suez Canal
Union with Syria in the United Arab Republic
Defeat in the Six-Day War

leaders.name: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk
leaders.summary: Founder of the Turkish republic who imposed a sweeping secular and nationalist modernisation under one party.

record.event: Founded the Republic of Turkey
Abolished the caliphate
Replaced Arabic script with the Latin alphabet
Women given the vote

leaders.name: Lee Kuan Yew
leaders.summary: Built Singapore into a rich trading hub under tightly controlled one-party-dominant rule.

record.event: Operation Coldstore: opponents detained without trial
Led Singapore to independence
Introduced national service
Mass public housing and a free-trade, export-led economy

leaders.name: Fidel Castro
leaders.summary: Revolutionary who built a one-party communist state with universal healthcare and education.

record.event: Took power in the Cuban Revolution
National literacy campaign; repelled the Bay of Pigs invasion
Cuban Missile Crisis
Handed power to his brother Raúl

leaders.name: Salvador Allende
leaders.summary: Marxist elected president who nationalised copper and was overthrown in a military coup.

record.event: Elected president
Copper nationalised by a unanimous vote of Congress
Overthrown in a military coup and died

leaders.name: Augusto Pinochet
leaders.summary: Military dictator whose regime killed and tortured thousands while imposing free-market reforms.

record.event: Seized power in a coup
Free-market “shock treatment” advised by the “Chicago Boys”
Privatised pensions
Official commissions documented thousands killed, disappeared and tortured
